title: RegretMatchingPotential.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The mixed potential Φ(x,y)=xᵀPy on Δ_m×Δ_n is bilinear and need not be jointly concave; its negative therefore permits nonconvex constrained optimization.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/RegretMatchingPotential.lean: spec.admissible permits arbitrary P with entries in [0,B]; spec.successful specifies mixed strategies.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Finite two-player exact-potential game with payoff matrices G₁,G₂ ∈ ℝ^{m×n}. A common potential matrix P reproduces every unilateral payoff difference. The target is an ε-Nash equilibrium, without a zero-sum assumption.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact full-information payoff-vector oracle: one call at any real vectors (x,y) returns (G₁y,G₂ᵀx). Replies are independent of call index and seed. No potential values or payoff matrices are directly supplied. Public parameters are m,n,ε; B is hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/RegretMatchingPotential.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Positive integers m,n define finite action sets and strategy spaces ℝ^m×ℝ^n; feasible outputs lie in Δ_m×Δ_n.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: There exists P with 0≤Pᵢⱼ≤B, B>0, such that G₁ᵢⱼ−G₁ᵢ′ⱼ=Pᵢⱼ−Pᵢ′ⱼ and G₂ᵢⱼ−G₂ᵢⱼ′=Pᵢⱼ−Pᵢⱼ′. Thus the potential range is at most B, while strategically irrelevant payoff offsets need not be bounded by B.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: Both output vectors are coordinatewise nonnegative and each sums exactly to one.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: Success is required for every ω, including every algorithm and oracle seed realization, rather than only in expectation or almost surely. The oracle-call budget is a fixed worst-case bound.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: For ε>0, the returned strategy pair satisfies max_i(G₁y)ᵢ−xᵀG₁y≤ε and max_j(G₂ᵀx)ⱼ−xᵀG₂y≤ε. This is an ε-Nash equilibrium of the output pair.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Approximate Nash equilibrium computation in finite exact-potential games with exact full payoff-vector feedback is an established standard formulation.

descriptionHtml:
Regret Matching+ in Potential Games

We consider a two-player game with payoff matrices A,C∈Rm×n, where m,n≥1 are the players’ numbers of actions. Mixed strategies are probability vectors in Rm and Rn. Unilateral payoff differences agree with those of an exact potential taking values in [0,B], where B>0. The oracle returns Ay and C⊤x at a strategy pair (x,y). For ε>0, Regret Matching+ must return probability vectors (x¯,y¯) for which neither player can increase its expected payoff by more than ε through any unilateral pure-action deviation.

Write Δd={z∈Rd:zi≥0 for all i, ∑i=1dzi=1}. The players maximize the respective payoffs x⊤Ay and x⊤Cy over x∈Δm and y∈Δn. The algorithm receives only m, n, and ε; the bound B may enter the oracle-call budget but is not an algorithm input.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Bounded exact potential). There exists a matrix H∈Rm×n such that, for all i,i′∈{1,…,m} and j,j′∈{1,…,n}, 0≤Hij≤B,Aij−Ai′j=Hij−Hi′j,Cij−Cij′=Hij−Hij′.

Queries may be made at any (x,y)∈Rm×Rn. One oracle call returns both exact payoff vectors ui=∑j=1nAijyj,i=1,…,m,vj=∑i=1mCijxi,j=1,…,n.

The setup is algorithm-specific: we analyze Regret Matching+ with simultaneous updates and retention of the most recent pair passing the deviation test. For d≥1 and q∈Rd, define Sd(q)i={qi/∑ℓ=1dqℓ,∑ℓ=1dqℓ>0,1/d,∑ℓ=1dqℓ≤0. Initialize the two regret vectors as q0=0∈Rm and r0=0∈Rn, and initialize the retained pair as z0=(Sm(0),Sn(0)). At iteration t≥0, query xt=Sm(qt),yt=Sn(rt),ut=Ayt,vt=C⊤xt. Define the instantaneous deviation gains and update the regret vectors by ait=uit−(xt)⊤ut,qit+1=max{qit+ait,0},bjt=vjt−(yt)⊤vt,rjt+1=max{rjt+bjt,0}. The retained pair is updated using the strategies queried at that iteration: zt+1={(xt,yt),ait≤ε for every i and bjt≤ε for every j,zt,otherwise. After the allotted T oracle calls, the output is (x¯,y¯)=zT. Thus, if no queried pair passes the test, the output remains the initial uniform pair.

The required accuracy is an ε-Nash equilibrium: x¯∈Δm,y¯∈Δn,(Ay¯)i≤x¯⊤Ay¯+ε,i=1,…,m,(C⊤x¯)j≤x¯⊤Cy¯+ε,j=1,…,n. These requirements hold for every realization, rather than only in expectation or almost surely.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Dov Monderer and Lloyd S. Shapley. Potential Games. 1996. Complexity: O(1+B/ε) paired payoff-vector oracle calls for ε-improvement dynamics to obtain a pure ε-Nash equilibrium, including the final check; deterministic worst-case cost.
  • Ioannis Anagnostides, Emanuel Tewolde, Brian Hu Zhang, Ioannis Panageas, Vincent Conitzer, and Tuomas Sandholm. Convergence of Regret Matching in Potential Games and Constrained Optimization. 2026 (preprint 2025; published version used). Complexity: O(1+max{m,n}B2/ε2) paired payoff-vector oracle calls for ε-lazy alternating discounted regret matching⁺ with fixed discount factor 1/2, obtaining an ε-Nash equilibrium; deterministic worst-case cost including initialization and equilibrium checks.
theorems.formulaHtml: ⌈20000⋅B2⋅(m+n)4ε2⌉++1

comparisonHtml:
Two-player exact potential games with m,n≥1, B,ε>0, payoff matrices A,C, and an exact potential P∈[0,B]m×n: unilateral payoff differences equal potential differences; payoff levels are unrestricted. Each oracle call returns (Ay,C⊤x) exactly. The setup fixes zero-initialized, undiscounted simultaneous RM+; public inputs are m,n,ε, while B determines the horizon. Its saved certified pre-update profile (x,y)∈Δm×Δn satisfies maxi(Ay)i−x⊤Ay≤ε and maxj(C⊤x)j−x⊤Cy≤ε for every seed. Prior methods are compared on these games in paired-vector calls; alternating sweeps cost two calls.

Comparison for RegretMatchingPotential.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) RegretMatchingPotential (Ours) (review) O(1+B2(m+n)4ε2)
(2) ε-lazy discounted alternating RM+ (Anagnostides et al. 2025, Cor. 3.5), γ=1/2 O(1+B2max(m,n)ε2) (1): Analysis of plain simultaneous RM+, with uniformly bounded regret states; no equilibrium-computation improvement. (1): Dimension factor (m+n)4 instead of max(m,n); only two players instead of arbitrary player counts.
(3) ε-lazy alternating RM+ (Anagnostides et al. 2025, Thm. 3.4) O(1+B4max(m,n)2ε4) (1): ε−2 instead of ε−4; smaller bound when 0<ε<Bmax(m,n)/(m+n)2. Always-updating simultaneous play. (1): Larger bound above that threshold for ε≤B; only two players.
(4) Zero-initialized ε-lazy simultaneous RM+ (Anagnostides et al. 2025, Thm. 3.12, App. C.1)

Derived bound on these games:

O(1+B8(m+n)10ε8), 0<ε≤B.

 (1): Dominant bound smaller by B6(m+n)6/ε6 for 0<ε≤B; no lazy skipping. (1): Only two-player bilinear potentials; (4) also covers smooth objectives on arbitrary products of simplices.
(5) Matrix recovery and potential maximization (Monderer and Shapley 1996, Lem. 2.1) Derived bound: O(max(m,n)); exact pure Nash equilibrium, using paired basis queries and uncharged arithmetic. (1): No established improvement in equilibrium computation; analyzes simultaneous RM+ rather than centralized reconstruction. (1): Larger bound for 0<ε≤B; only approximate mixed-profile accuracy, not exact pure equilibrium.
(6) Unilateral improvement (Monderer and Shapley 1996, Lem. 4.2) Derived bound: O(1+B/ε); pure ε-Nash profile, one paired call per tested profile. (1): No established complexity improvement; analyzes simultaneous RM+ without coordinating unilateral deviations. (1): Larger bound for 0<ε≤B; does not guarantee a pure profile.

Abbr: Δd is the probability simplex on d actions; RM+ is regret matching with nonnegative clipping; γ is the geometric discount parameter. An ε-lazy update skips a player whose deviation gain is at most ε.

Anagnostides, Ioannis, Emanuel Tewolde, Brian Hu Zhang, Ioannis Panageas, Vincent Conitzer, and Tuomas Sandholm. 2025. Convergence of Regret Matching in Potential Games and Constrained Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2510.17067.
Monderer, Dov, and Lloyd S. Shapley. 1996. “Potential Games.” Games and Economic Behavior 14 (1): 124–43. https://doi.org/10.1006/game.1996.0044.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin

namespace OracleTemplate.RegretMatchingPotential

noncomputable def total {m : ℕ} (Q : Fin m → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ a, Q a

noncomputable def strategy {m : ℕ} (Q : Fin m → ℝ) : Fin m → ℝ :=
  if 0 < total Q then fun a => Q a / total Q else fun _ => 1 / (m : ℝ)

noncomputable def value {m : ℕ} (x u : Fin m → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ a, x a * u a

noncomputable def regret {m : ℕ} (Q u : Fin m → ℝ) : Fin m → ℝ :=
  fun a => u a - value (strategy Q) u

noncomputable def step {m : ℕ} (Q u : Fin m → ℝ) : Fin m → ℝ :=
  fun a => max (Q a + regret Q u a) 0

open Classical in
noncomputable def rmPlusPotential (m n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) :
    Algorithm ((Fin m → ℝ) × (Fin n → ℝ)) ((Fin m → ℝ) × (Fin n → ℝ))
      ((Fin m → ℝ) × (Fin n → ℝ)) where
  State := (Fin m → ℝ) × (Fin n → ℝ) × ((Fin m → ℝ) × (Fin n → ℝ))
  initial _ := (0, 0, (strategy 0, strategy 0))
  query s := (0, (strategy s.1, strategy s.2.1))
  update s r := (step s.1 r.1, step s.2.1 r.2,
    if (∀ a, regret s.1 r.1 a ≤ ε) ∧ ∀ b, regret s.2.1 r.2 b ≤ ε then
      (strategy s.1, strategy s.2.1) else s.2.2)
  output s := s.2.2

end OracleTemplate.RegretMatchingPotential

namespace LongTails.Setups.RegretMatchingPotential

open OracleTemplate OracleTemplate.RegretMatchingPotential

structure Public where
  m : ℕ
  n : ℕ
  ε : ℝ

structure Params extends Public where
  B : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := (Fin p.m → Fin p.n → ℝ) × (Fin p.m → Fin p.n → ℝ)
  Query p := (Fin p.m → ℝ) × (Fin p.n → ℝ)
  Reply p := (Fin p.m → ℝ) × (Fin p.n → ℝ)
  Output p := (Fin p.m → ℝ) × (Fin p.n → ℝ)
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.m ∧ 0 < q.n ∧ 0 < q.B ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q G oracle :=
    (∃ P : Fin q.m → Fin q.n → ℝ, (∀ i j, 0 ≤ P i j ∧ P i j ≤ q.B) ∧
      (∀ i i' j, G.1 i j - G.1 i' j = P i j - P i' j) ∧
      ∀ i j j', G.2 i j - G.2 i j' = P i j - P i j') ∧
    ∀ k x y seed, oracle.answer k (0, (x, y)) seed =
      (fun i => ∑ j, G.1 i j * y j, fun j => ∑ i, G.2 i j * x i)
  successful q G output _ :=
    ∀ ω, let x := (output ω).1
      let y := (output ω).2
      (∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) ∧ ∑ i, x i = 1 ∧ (∀ j, 0 ≤ y j) ∧ ∑ j, y j = 1 ∧
      (∀ i, ∑ j, G.1 i j * y j ≤ ∑ i', ∑ j, x i' * G.1 i' j * y j + q.ε) ∧
      ∀ j, ∑ i, x i * G.2 i j ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j', x i * G.2 i j' * y j' + q.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p algorithm := algorithm = rmPlusPotential p.m p.n p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.RegretMatchingPotential
